Round 2 · Implementation · Hard

Ticket #24 — Multi-Location Inventory

Difficulty: Hard

Context

You maintain stock transfers between shop locations. On-hand stock can be sold at a location. In-transit units have left the source but have not yet been received by the destination. The local ledger tracks each transfer ID through one terminal outcome: received or cancelled.

Practice report

Start with 8 books at east and 2 at west. Call start("t1", "book", "east", "west", 3), then receive t1 once.

Observation after receipt Current starter Expected
East on-hand books 5 5
West on-hand books 8 5
Transfer state received received

On a fresh repository, start and cancel the same transfer instead. The expected final stock is the original 8 and 2, with the transfer marked cancelled.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Starting a valid transfer removes units from source on-hand stock and records exactly one in_transit transfer. Destination on-hand stock is unchanged until receipt.
  • Receipt adds the transfer's units to destination stock once and changes it to received. Cancellation instead restores source stock once and changes it to cancelled without a destination credit.
  • Only an in-transit transfer can be received or cancelled. Repeated receipt, repeated cancellation, and crossing from one terminal outcome to the other are rejected without further effects.
  • Reject missing IDs/SKU/locations, duplicate transfer IDs, same source and destination, invalid nonpositive/non-integer quantities, booleans, and insufficient source stock without changing stock or transfer history.
  • Across all transfers of a SKU, on-hand units plus in-transit units are conserved. Each transfer has exactly one terminal outcome.

Out of Scope

Use the in-memory ledger and supplied location names. Carrier tracking, shipping systems, damaged goods, and partial receipts are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Trace start, receive, and cancellation through the two scenarios described above. Add assertions for both locations before and after each transition, terminal-state rejection, and conservation with several transfers in transit.
